answer: Sybils are cheap to mint but costly to keep awake. Give every identity unpredictable spot-checks bound to the seed that must be answered inside a two-second window. One agent passes its own check easily; an operator running a hundred clones on shared hardware queues up and misses windows. Reject the fable that cheap clones are harmless: grade standing by latency, current through copper, so on-time identities keep full weight while latecomers drain through the inlet of zero influence. Cloning stops paying: the bottleneck is the operator's own machine.
